verdict.rationale: Working Copy's manual documents both halves of the story. An Amend toggle in the commit dialog changes the latest commit, and swiping left undoes unpushed commits while leaving their changes in the working directory. Hunk-level staging then lets you recommit those changes as separate, split commits, and long-press history edits (edit message, squash, delete) add further fix-up options. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the amend/undo/split workflow.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can amend the latest commit or undo unpushed commits to fix or split them

citations.quote: To make changes to the latest commit enable Amend at the top of the commit dialog.
For commits not yet pushed to a remote, swipe left to Undo them. The commit's changes remain in your working directory as modified files
you can stage/unstage individual hunks by long-tapping and swiping making it possible to commit some changes in a file but leave others uncommitted.
Edit Message to change a commit message... or Squash a commit with its child.
